title: Geometric components of an affine scheme descend to a finite constant extension
statement:
Fix a prime power $q$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be an affine scheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum] of finite type over $k_0$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ [def-pc-base-change]. There exist an integer $e\geq1$ and a finite set $I$ such that, with $k_e=\mathbf F_{q^e}\subset k$, there is a decomposition into nonempty open and closed affine subschemes
$$X_0\times_{k_0}k_e=\coprod_{i\in I}X_{i,e}.$$
Each $X_{i,e}$ is geometrically connected over $k_e$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and their base changes to $k$ are exactly the connected components of $X$ [def-weil-connected-scheme]. If $X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is smooth of relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], each $X_{i,e}\to\operatorname{Spec}k_e$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$. The empty scheme is allowed, with $I=\varnothing$.

proof.text: Let X be the base change to k. Finite type survives base change by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. The spectrum of a field is Noetherian; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] therefore makes X Noetherian. This uses Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.Noetherian directly, without writing an affine tensor-product presentation.

proof.text: Index the components by I = ConnectedComponents X. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-connected-components-open] this type is finite and each fibre of the quotient map is open. Choose a representative r(i) in each fibre, which is the nonempty connected set connectedComponent(r(i)) by [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Its compactness follows from [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets]. This construction works when X is empty: I is then empty.

source.place: Tag 038E, lemma-galois-action-connected-components-continuous, statement and proof (components descend to finite subextensions); Tag 0387, lemma-characterize-geometrically-connected; morphisms.tex Tags 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth), 02NK (lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d)

proof.text: For each component open apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-qc-open-fg-subalgebra]. A finitely generated subalgebra of the algebraic extension k/k_0 [def-weil-algebraic-closure] is finite over k_0: its finitely many algebra generators are integral, so their algebra is module-finite, as in [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension]. Being a finite-dimensional domain over a field it is a field, hence gives a finite intermediate field. Take the supremum of the finitely many intermediate fields; it is still finite. Pull every descended open back to this common field. Functoriality of baseChangeMap [def-pc-base-change] shows that their preimages over k are the original opens.

source.place: Tag 038E, lemma-galois-action-connected-components-continuous, statement and proof (components descend to finite subextensions); Tag 0387, lemma-characterize-geometrically-connected; morphisms.tex Tags 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth), 02NK (lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d)

proof.text: Put e = finrank(k_0,L), which is positive, and compute Nat.card L = q^e using the finite-dimensional cardinality formula. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure] identifies its subfield with D.extensionSubfield e he. The subfield equality gives the comparison algebra map L to this specified field; compatibility of its inclusion with extensionEmbedding gives the scalar-extension projection p. By [def-pc-base-change] its square with the two structure maps is cartesian, and its composite with the first projection is the first projection upstairs.

source.place: Tag 038E, lemma-galois-action-connected-components-continuous, statement and proof (components descend to finite subextensions); Tag 0387, lemma-characterize-geometrically-connected; morphisms.tex Tags 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth), 02NK (lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d)

proof.text: The field-spectrum map is surjective by [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective], so its scheme base change p is surjective. This is the general Mathlib base-change stability of Surjective and does not require an affine spectrum calculation. If W_i denotes the descended open, membership p(x) in W_i is equivalent to ConnectedComponents.mk x = i. Surjectivity therefore proves that the W_i cover and are pairwise disjoint. Each W_i is nonempty because it contains p(r(i)). Its complement is the union of W_j for j different from i, hence open, so W_i is closed.

source.place: Tag 038E, lemma-galois-action-connected-components-continuous, statement and proof (components descend to finite subextensions); Tag 0387, lemma-characterize-geometrically-connected; morphisms.tex Tags 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth), 02NK (lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d)

proof.text: Take X_{i,e} to be W_i with its restricted scheme structure. Its inclusion is an open immersion; since its range is closed it is also a closed immersion (IsClosedImmersion.of_isPreimmersion). A closed immersion into an affine scheme has affine source by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion]. Thus no idempotent/basic-open construction is needed. The inclusions, coverage, and disjointness give exactly the decomposition recorded by AffineGeometricComponentDecomposition.

source.place: Tag 038E, lemma-galois-action-connected-components-continuous, statement and proof (components descend to finite subextensions); Tag 0387, lemma-characterize-geometrically-connected; morphisms.tex Tags 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth), 02NK (lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d)

proof.text: Restrict p to the inverse image of each W_i. The restriction square is cartesian, and pasting it with the scalar-extension square [def-pc-base-change] identifies that open subscheme with the pullback of X_{i,e} to k. This is also the restricted-scheme base change of the open inclusion [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. Use the inverse comparison isomorphism followed by the open inclusion to define baseComponent. The pullback projection identities prove both prescribed projection equations. Its range is the original component open, and the image of the chosen componentPoint is r(i); thus component_range holds, and components_bijective is the identity of I under the representative equations. The pullback is connected because it is isomorphic to the connected component. The field k is algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure]; applying [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure] over the finite field proves geometric connectedness.

proof.text: Given SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f_0, install the base-change stability from [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] to obtain the property for the second projection. Open immersions are smooth of relative dimension zero by the Mathlib instance for [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Compose using smoothOfRelativeDimension_comp and simplify zero plus d. The inclusion_over equation identifies this composite with componentMap.
